decision: Numeric one-run 18 GiB prelaunch exception passes; actual host-memory adequacy is not established. Do not launch WSL, load the model, import the native runtime or run the forward under these readings.
scope: Independent read-only review of saved source-safe CPU qualification, actual historical successful WSL worker/supervisor reports and Windows RAM samples. Only this report is written. No tests, WSL, Torch, native runtime, GPU, model payload loading or network operation occurred in this review.

closest_historical_successful_F16_PBR.same_model_contract: 284 parameters, 208 F16 / 76 F32; 948567448 runtime parameter bytes

actual_Windows_available_RAM_samples.stage: lowest whole-attempt sampled Windows availability, while holding output before host readback acknowledgement

closest_historical_successful_F16_PBR.measurement_limits: The Windows declines are measured whole-host changes correlated with stages, not causally isolated WSL consumption. One-second samples are not a continuous physical-memory bound. Worker RSS/HWM measures one guest process; it is neither full process-tree memory nor Windows available RAM. The guest MemAvailable value is not Windows availability. No complete host/guest process-tree peak or vmmem committed baseline is present in these saved reports. No current vmmem commitment measurement was made. No current GPU measurement was made.

other_actual_successful_WSL_reports.workload: turret BF16 geometry decoder with saved genuine output
brick BF16 geometry decoder with saved genuine output

brick_visible_payloads_not_a_host_peak_b.contract: 284 parameters, 208 F16 / 76 F32; six large F16 sites, 84 tiles plus 60 final tiles
brick_visible_payloads_not_a_host_peak_b.limitation: These are intrinsic payload sizes, not additive independent ownership claims or a bound on CPU copies, strict-loader transient RSS, runtime imports, WSL VM/kernel/cache retention, pinned transfers, output serialization or independent Windows readback. The CPU source review's 3230157582-byte retained envelope and 8968476420-byte padded projection concern device-visible tensors and explicitly do not bound host RAM. Brick has larger support and adds six large-site tiling lifecycles; turret host peaks cannot be asserted as upper bounds for it.

adequacy_arithmetic.interpretation: This is a counterfactual screen, not a prediction or a causal WSL estimate. Even the best fresh reading would be 606445568 bytes below the unchanged live floor if the closest successful F16 PBR trace's whole-host decline recurred. At exactly 18 GiB the observed pre-GPU decline alone leaves only 4382720 bytes above the floor. The evidence therefore does not justify a conditional launch or a model-load experiment at current headroom. Smaller declines in other successful geometry runs do not establish a material-decoder upper bound.

precise_evidence_gap: No measured WSL VM/process-tree commitment baseline and no upper bound on remaining host physical-memory demand for the exact brick F16 loader, guides, tiled forward, output serialization and independent readback. Single-process CPU HWM and device tensor projections cannot close this gap. Monitoring can detect a breach after it happens; it does not establish that the next allocation can preserve the floor.
minimum_pre_forward_checks_for_any_later: Start healthy Windows GlobalMemoryStatusEx monitoring before WSL startup; retain actual physical availability and separate commit/process-tree/vmmem observations. Require fresh admission before marker reservation and every stage barrier.

Place an explicit host-controlled stop barrier after WSL/runtime import and again after strict model/input/guide loading, before GPU placement or forward. Do not proceed if remaining measured headroom cannot cover independently justified remaining host demand; the historical values above are observations, not a new global gate or proven bound.

Refuse the next stage while a measured downward trend or next known allocation would approach the 12884901888-byte live floor; fail closed on stale/failed monitoring. Keep the existing floor, unchanged VRAM caps/reserves and deadlines. The present evidence does not supply a defensible extra safety buffer, so none is invented here.
policy_effect: None. This report refuses adequacy for the requested one-run exception under current readings; it changes no historical default or source policy.
